chapter: Desvigne, Chicago offers and Peter Hone's band
title: Don Albert's offer versus the Desvigne boat job
summary: Albert tries to hire him for his new band, but Sayles, sick and short of money, takes a salaried boat season with Sidney Desvigne.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: Took men out of Sydney's band? Who's Sydney? Sydney Desby.

I see. Yeah, I believe he took one of the, Herbert Hall out of that band, a saxophone player. And, uh, he had a band, well, he can, he can hear you going all around. Well, he came to me, and, uh, told me about the deal. Well, I was kind of a little sick then, and my wife then was working as a waitress at the Pelican, and I was working up there on that story. And, uh, I had an offer to Sydney Desby to go on the boat, see. The season on the boat opens up around, I think around about April and May. So, I thought about it, I say, uh, I had worked on the boat with Fate, and I say, I know that's pretty good money. I mean, you know, in other words, it's a job you know you're going to get paid, you don't have to worry, and you stay there, you live, your expense don't cost you nothing, you get your straight salary, you know. And I said, well, this will give me a little chance to kind of get out of the hole, you know. And, uh, so, I tried everything. He was, he wanted to give me, like, he was giving fellas $20, and some guys he gave $50, you know, to go away with him. But, I didn't, I didn't take that deal with him. And, uh, well, I don't go away from the man that was down. Well, anyhow, I went on the boat. Well, when I went on the boat, uh, Danny Barker was working up on, uh, on a place on, on, on, on, on the canal in Burgundy, with, uh, with Willie Pajo and a woman, you see, I believe Sonny, Sonny was on the trombone, I believe Saeed was on the drum up there, and another fella got killed, John something clown that, he plays clown that, he got killed, yeah, in California. And, uh.
